AbstractText.Label: STUDY QUESTION
AbstractText.content: What is the prevalence of leiomyosarcomas and atypical leiomyomas after laparoscopic morcellation of fibroids in reproductive age women?

AbstractText.Label: SUMMARY ANSWER
AbstractText.content: No case of leiomyosarcomas but seven atypical leiomyomas were found in 1216 subjects.

AbstractText.Label: WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY
AbstractText.content: Although uterine sarcoma is a rare entity affecting usually older peri- or post-menopausal women, the Food and Drug Administration discourages use of laparoscopic power morcellation of uterine fibroids.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION
AbstractText.content: Retrospective review of data extracted from a single center database of 1216 consecutive women who underwent laparoscopic morcellation of 2582 unsuspicious leiomyomas between June 2003 and December 2015 and were followed-up until December 2016.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTINGS, METHODS
AbstractText.content: A total of 1216 women, aged 18-45 years, underwent laparoscopic morcellation of 2582 apparently benign leiomyomas by the same surgeon and all specimen slides were examined by the same experienced pathologist.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE
AbstractText.content: The prevalence of leiomyosarcomas and atypical leiomyomas was 0% (95% CI: 0-0.3%) and 0.6% (95% CI: 0.23-1.18%) (six atypical-bizarre and one mitotically active leiomyoma) respectively. In addition, there were identified 34 cases of adenomyomas, 45 leiomyomas with infarcts, 81 cellular leiomyomas and 133 degenerated leiomyomas. No morcellator-associated complication was recorded and none of the patients included in this study required conversion to laparotomy.

AbstractText.Label: LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION
AbstractText.content: Retrospective and single referral center study design.

AbstractText.Label: WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS
AbstractText.content: Laparoscopic morcellation of unsuspicious leiomyomas after careful preoperative work up seems to be safe in women of reproductive age.
